extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia editors (particularly those who edit or create mathematics articles)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating, editing, and maintaining mathematics articles on Wikipedia, including style, sourcing, dispute resolution, and handling vandalism. Targeted at contributors working within WikiProject Mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be bold but not reckless
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are encouraged to be bold, but not reckless, in editing articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If something seems wrong, feel free to fix it or move it to a talk page for discussion. If an article or section needs to be rewritten, or if you have something to add, feel free to do so yourself. Other editors will often respond to an initial change by editing the article themselves, so even a few small edits can lead to significant improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the intended reader in mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Write with the target reader's background and needs in mind; different topics require different levels of exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main point in writing any article is to keep the intended reader in mind; an article on Fermat's Last Theorem is very different than an article on étale cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the five pillars of Wikipedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to Wikipedia's core principles that guide content and community behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five pillars of Wikipedia contain the general principles guiding the encyclopedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure verifiability and cite reliable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Material in articles must be attributable to reliable sources and meet Wikipedia's verifiability standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is important that material in articles can be attributed to reliable sources. There are encyclopedia-wide policies requiring verifiability of article content. The scientific citation guidelines explain the ideals we have for attribution in mathematics articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include original research
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must not contain original research or unpublished claims presented as fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wikipedia policies prohibit many forms of original research; content should be based on published, reliable sources rather than novel proofs or unpublished results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Manual of Style for mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Wikipedia Manual of Style (general and mathematics) to structure articles and adopt appropriate writing conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Wikipedia Manual of Style for mathematics offers useful suggestions on how to structure a mathematics article, as well as on the writing style and many other issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve content disputes by discussion and consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreements about article content should be resolved via talk-page discussion aiming for consensus rather than by unilateral changes or votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different editors will often have different opinions about the proper content of an article. The way to resolve such disagreements is by discussion; the content of articles is decided by consensus rather than voting. Previous discussion in the talk page archives of the article may show how the article came to its present state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repeated reverts; observe the three-revert rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not repeatedly revert another editor's edits; repeated reversion can lead to sanctions under the three-revert rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In every case, avoid repeatedly reverting the edits of another editor (except in case of obvious vandalism). It is unproductive for reaching consensus and can lead to you being blocked under the three-revert rule if continued. The essay WP:BRD describes one strategy for finding consensus on the content of an article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report serial or persistent problematic editing (WP:AN3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an editor repeatedly adds or removes the same material (more than three reversions at a single page within 24 hours), this may be reported for further action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some editors repeatedly add the same material to a single article despite consensus against doing so. If any editor makes more than three reversions to the same article within a 24 hour period, this may be reported at WP:AN3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalate complex issues to administrators (WP:ANI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex or serious disputes that require detailed analysis should be reported to administrators for intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More complex situations that require a detailed analysis by an administrator may be reported at WP:ANI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle vandalism promptly and proportionately
rubrics_metrics.description: One-off vandalism should be reverted; persistent vandalism should be warned and may be escalated to blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For one-time vandalism to a single page, the best solution is to revert it and forget it. There is no requirement to report it anywhere. If you wish, you may place a warning template message on the user's talk page. Editors who deface many pages in a short period of time, or who repeatedly vandalize a single page, may be blocked if they do not appear likely to stop vandalizing. Blocks are intended only to slow down vandalism, not to punish editors; a typical block for vandalism will last no more than 24 hours. If the editor continues to vandalize after a high-level template is placed, the editor may be reported at WP:AIV, where an administrator will decide whether to block the user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate warning templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Warn problematic users with the correct templates before escalating to administrative action where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish, you may place a warning template message on the user's talk page. These warning messages let other editors know that the user has engaged in vandalism before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt math-specific syntax and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow mathematics conventions for formulas, symbols, naming, and character usage to ensure clarity and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References given include: Manual of style: general, mathematics; Formulas; Unicode character table; Mathematics conventions; Naming conventions: general, theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create clear figures, graphs, and diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Use well-constructed visual aids to illustrate mathematical ideas where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a section on creating graphs and diagrams to help with figures in mathematics articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow referencing and citation best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the recommended reference resources and follow scientific citation guidelines for mathematics content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referencing: Reference resources and Scientific citation guideline are listed as tools and standards to follow for attribution in mathematics articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available editor tools and UI customizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Customize your editing environment with CSS and JavaScript and consider helpful extensions to improve the editing experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can customize many aspects of the user interface using CSS and JavaScript. CSS customization and JavaScript customization are linked. Popups — a JavaScript extension that many editors find helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply special care for biographies of living persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Biography articles about living people are subject to special sourcing and content rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special guidelines apply to biographies of living persons.
